episode.title: Productization (Again)
episode.description: Productization is a compression of something you already do well and repeatedly. David and Blair on why most firms package too early, and what that does to pricing.

head.label: A
head.text: Welcome back to 2Bobs. I'm Blair Enns, and as always I'm joined by David C. Baker.

head.label: A
head.text: Today we are returning to productization, which is a subject we have circled more than once.

head.label: B
head.text: We have, and I think we keep coming back to it because most firms get the sequencing wrong.

head.label: B
head.text: They productize before they have any real evidence that the market wants the thing they are packaging.

head.label: A
head.text: So the failure is not packaging as such. The failure is packaging too early.

head.label: B
head.text: Right. Productization is a compression of something you already do well and repeatedly.

head.label: B
head.text: If you have not done it repeatedly, there is nothing to compress.

head.label: A
head.text: Let us talk about pricing, because that is where I see the most damage.

head.label: A
head.text: The moment you put a fixed price on a productized offering, you have capped your upside.

head.label: B
head.text: Unless the cost of delivery falls faster than the price does.

head.label: A
head.text: Which is the whole argument for productizing in the first place.

head.label: B
head.text: It is. And it is why I would rather see a firm productize the diagnostic than the delivery.
